title: Study of localization properties under subsystem periodic driving
authors: Arpita Goswami, Ranjan Modak, Shaon Sahoo
abstract: Periodic driving provides a powerful route for controlling localization and engineering effective Hamiltonians in quantum systems. A localized one-dimensional Aubry-André chain can be driven into a fully delocalized phase when the entire system is driven below a critical frequency. Here, we ask whether such delocalization can be achieved by driving only a part of the system. We address this question using a two-leg ladder comprising an Aubry-André chain coupled to a periodically driven clean tight-binding chain. Exact numerical calculations show that, starting from a localized static ladder, subsystem driving below a critical frequency cannot achieve complete delocalization. Instead, a mixed phase emerges, with localized and delocalized states coexisting and the fraction of delocalized states varying nonmonotonically with the driving frequency. This behavior can be understood using local effective Hamiltonians. Although these effective Hamiltonians are derived analytically in the high-frequency regime, they can nevertheless predict the localization transition occurring in the moderate-frequency regime. In fact, by quantifying the emergent nonlocality of the Floquet Hamiltonian, we show that these effective Hamiltonians provide a valid description up to a crossover frequency that is lower than the critical frequency associated with the localization transition. Our results demonstrate an alternative route to Floquet engineering, in which the transport properties of a quantum lattice system can be modified by driving only a subsystem.
summary: This work explores the localization properties of a quantum ladder system driven periodically by only a subsystem. The authors find that such partial driving cannot fully delocalize a localized state, instead creating a mixed phase of coexisting localized and delocalized states. This demonstrates an alternative, subsystem-controlled route for modifying quantum transport properties.
main_problem: The study investigates whether periodic driving of only a subsystem in a quantum lattice can induce complete delocalization, contrasting this with driving the entire system.
main_result: Subsystem driving below a critical frequency cannot achieve full delocalization, instead leading to a mixed phase where localized and delocalized states coexist nonmonotonically.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory to derive the effective Hamiltonian and uses exact numerical diagonalization of the Floquet operator to characterize the localization properties.
model_or_system: The model is a two-leg ladder system combining an Aubry-André chain and a clean tight-binding chain, subjected to a periodic square-wave drive applied only to one leg.
key_observables: Fraction of delocalized states, state-averaged Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and the decay profile of inter-leg coupling amplitudes $C(r)$.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega$), critical frequency ($\omega_c$), and the ratio of driving frequency to system parameters.
main_assumptions: The effective Hamiltonians are derived analytically in the high-frequency regime but are shown to predict the transition physics even in the moderate-frequency regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic model setup and show the evolution of the IPR and the non-locality decay $C(r)$ as a function of driving frequency.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the driven Hamiltonian and applying Floquet theory to calculating localization diagnostics (IPR) and non-locality measures ($C(r)$), culminating in the demonstration of the mixed-phase behavior.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete example of how localized states can be manipulated by local driving fields, offering insights into Floquet engineering beyond global driving protocols.
